newsitem.title: USA: Slim WTI/Brent buoys U.S. domestic, Latam crudes.
newsitem.headline: Slim WTI/Brent buoys U.S. domestic, Latam crudes.

text.p: The spread between U.S. and North Sea benchmark crudes remained slim on Monday, buoying U.S. domestic and Latin American grades, traders said.

The August spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent was around $1.35-45 a barrel, about five cents wider than last Thursday but still narrow enough to discourage trans-Atlantic activity.
Among the sparse offerings was Norwegian Heidrun for mid-August delivery into the Gulf at September WTI minus $1.00 a barrel, traders said.
Brent was notionally assessed around 20-25 cents under WTI, a level that drove most U.S. refiners to shop around closer to home.
"It's still difficult to make sense out of bringing (Brent) over right now," a Gulf Coast trader said.
The continued dearth of North Sea sweet grades in the thirsty U.S. Gulf was reflected in the strengthening discount for Colombian Cusiana.
The gasoline-rich grade changed hands last week at 90-95 cents under WTI, but was assessed five to 10 cents stronger on Monday.
Softening freight rates in the Caribbean have also brightened Cusiana's appeal, traders said.
Seven cargoes of Cusiana are left for August, with British Petroleum holding the next cargo loading August 12-16.
U.S. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James also got a lift out of the narrow arb, trading around 19-22 cents premium to WTI/Cushing.
Meanwhile, regional sour grades were particularly active as traders await the resumption of Iraqi humanitarian oil sales.
A trading house sold an Oriente cargo for August 14-17 arrival into the U.S. at $3.10-15 under WTI, a few pennies firmer than an August 10-15 Oriente transacted last week.
Separately, a European company sold a Cano Limon cargo out of Colombia at around $2.35 a barrel under WTI on an fob basis.
Also out of Colombia, a Swiss trader late last week sold a Vasconia cargo loading August 14-19 at around $3.15 a barrel under WTI fob, traders said.
Finally, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP bought one million barrels of Iranian Heavy crude last Thursday from Brazil's state oil company Petrobras for August 18-28 delivery.
ANCAP paid $1.20-30 under Dated Brent on a cost and freight basis, traders said.
